permit.applies: The worker applies, online, after a licensed sponsor (the engager) has assigned a certificate of sponsorship; the sponsor follows the Creative Worker code of practice for the role (advertising, or an exemption from it).
permit.first: A certificate of sponsorship from a licensed sponsor, assigned on the code of practice for performers (or workers) in film and television, theatre, opera, ballet or dance.

fees.what: Certificate of sponsorship, Temporary Worker (paid by the sponsor)
Priority visa service (decision usually within 5 working days)
Super priority visa service (decision usually by the end of the next working day)

permit.union: Equity: for a film or television performer engaged without advertising (commercially important to the production), the sponsor must give Equity prior notice with the role, the film and the reasons; for continuity where the performer worked on the production overseas less than a month, the sponsor must notify Equity at least 5 working days before issuing the certificate.
permit.eligibility: The job must be one where they will make a unique contribution to the UK’s rich cultural life.
permit.pay: Performers in film and television: payment must be at least at the level of the appropriate UK market rates, which can be obtained from Equity; the job and pay must comply with the National Minimum Wage.

sources.title: GOV.UK, Creative Worker visa (Temporary Work)
sources.said: you’ll usually get a decision on your visa within: 3 weeks, if you’re outside the UK 8 weeks, if you’re inside the UK … pay the healthcare surcharge , which is usually £1,035 per year … The application fee for each person applying is £340. … You can come to the UK for a maximum of up to 12 months, or the time given in your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter. You may be able to extend your visa .

sources.title: GOV.UK, Immigration Rules Appendix Temporary Work – Creative Worker
sources.said: A person can be granted permission for up to 12 months initially and can apply to extend their stay up to a maximum of two years if they are still working for the same sponsor. … details of the job and pay the sponsor is offering them confirming that these arrangements comply with the National Minimum Wage

sources.title: GOV.UK, Immigration Rules Appendix Creative Worker Codes of Practice
sources.said: Performers in film and television Appropriate salary rate Payment must be at least at the level of the appropriate UK market rates, which can be obtained from Equity at www.equity.org.uk. … the Sponsor must notify Equity at least 5 working days prior to the issuing of the certificate with details of the filming schedules. … The sponsor must give prior notice to Equity providing supporting evidence detailing: description of the role and film, and the reasons why advertising was not appropriate and a letter in support.

sources.title: GOV.UK, Workers and Temporary Workers: guidance for sponsors: Sponsor a Creative Worker
sources.said: CRW1.2. The job the Creative Worker is coming to do must be one where they will make a unique contribution to the UK’s rich cultural life. Areas covered include, but are not limited to, dance, music, film, theatre, television, circuses, opera and fashion modelling. … CRW5.6. You must pay a fee for each CoS you assign

sources.title: GOV.UK, Get a faster decision on your visa or settlement application
sources.said: You’ll need to pay £500 in addition to the application fee. Using the priority service means you’ll usually get a decision within 5 working days for most visa applications.

sources.title: GOV.UK, Immigration Rules Appendix Visitor: Permitted Activities
sources.said: PA 19. A Visitor may undertake the permitted paid engagements in V 13.3, providing they are completed within 30 days of the Visitor’s entry to the UK, and the requirements of V 13.1. to V 13.2. are met.
